character: The ultimate test of precision — narrow, unforgiving street circuit with barriers inches from the racing line. Track position and error-free driving matter more than outright pace. Slowest average speed on the calendar.
sources: https://www.formula1.com/en/racing/2026/monaco/circuit official F1 circuit guide; Sainte Devote/Massenet/Casino/Mirabeau/Grand Hotel Hairpin/Portier/Tabac/Swimming Pool/Rascasse/Antony Noghes naming long-established
notes: Meta (and the circuit's current sponsor) call T6 the Fairmont Hairpin. Meta calls T14-15 by its French name, Piscine.

corners.name: Sainte Devote
corners.technique: Hard braking from the start/finish straight, clean early apex to set up the climb to Massenet
corners.trap: Contact-prone on the opening lap; running wide costs the run up the hill

corners.name: Massenet
corners.technique: Commit through the blind crest, smooth steering, trust the line to Casino Square
corners.trap: Lifting on the blind crest loses momentum into Casino Square

corners.name: Casino Square
corners.technique: Ride the crest and camber changes with minimal steering correction
corners.trap: Bumps unsettle the car — over-correcting here compounds the problem

corners.name: Mirabeau
corners.technique: Firm braking on the downhill approach, late apex
corners.trap: Braking too late on the downhill and missing the apex

corners.name: Grand Hotel Hairpin
corners.type: slowest corner on the F1 calendar
corners.technique: Full steering lock, very low speed, precise placement to avoid the barriers
corners.trap: Clipping the barrier on entry or exit — almost zero margin for error

corners.name: Portier
corners.technique: Late apex, clean exit is essential before entering the tunnel at speed
corners.trap: Poor exit here compromises tunnel entry speed

corners.name: Nouvelle Chicane
corners.technique: Hard braking from tunnel speed, precise through the direction change
corners.trap: Braking too late after the tunnel — a common overtaking-crash point

corners.name: Tabac
corners.technique: Smooth commitment along the harbour wall
corners.trap: Any correction near the wall is highly costly

corners.name: Swimming Pool
corners.technique: Precise, rhythmic direction changes through the barriers with no margin
corners.trap: Overdriving any part of the complex risks wall contact

corners.name: Rascasse
corners.technique: Low speed, full commitment to the apex, patient throttle
corners.trap: Running wide on exit compromises the run to Antony Noghes

corners.name: Antony Noghes
corners.type: final corner onto the pit straight
corners.technique: Late apex, clean exit is critical — feeds the start/finish straight
corners.trap: Compromised exit costs time all the way to the line
